1. **`src/OrchardCore/OrchardCore.ContentManagement/ContentDefinitionManager.cs` — `DeleteTypeDefinitionAsync` / `DeletePartDefinitionAsync`**: Calling `LoadTypeDefinition(document, name)` / `LoadPartDefinition(document, name)` just to build the `*RemovedContext` populates the per-scope caches (`_scopedTypeDefinitions`/`_scopedPartDefinitions`) with the definition *before* the record is removed. Because `LoadTypeDefinitionAsync`/`LoadPartDefinitionAsync` check that scoped cache first, any subsequent call for that name within the same unit-of-work/request will return the stale, just-deleted definition instead of `null`. Build the event context from data already in hand (or bypass/evict the scoped cache entry) instead of routing through the memoizing `Load*` helper.

2. **Scope mismatch with the linked issue / PR description**: The description claims `ContentDefinitionService` was "updated to trigger events through `ContentDefinitionManager` instead of directly," but the diff contains no change to `ContentDefinitionService.cs`. Likewise, `ContentDefinitionManager` only triggers 3 of the ~15 new `IContentDefinitionHandler` event methods (Type/Part Created/Updated/Removed) — `ContentPartAttached/Detached`, `ContentTypeImporting/Imported`, `ContentPartImporting/Imported`, `ContentFieldAttached/Updated/Detached`, `ContentTypePartUpdated`, `ContentPartFieldUpdated` are added to the interface but never invoked from the manager. The actual goal of #16926 (stop `ContentDefinitionService` from owning event-triggering, centralize in the manager) is not achieved — this needs the real `ContentDefinitionService` changes and the remaining event wiring before merge.

3. **`test/OrchardCore.Tests/ContentDefinition/ContentDefinitionEventMigrationTests.cs`**: `MockContentDefinitionManager.StoreTypeDefinitionAsync`/`DeleteTypeDefinitionAsync` are no-ops (`Task.CompletedTask`) that never call the `Trigger*` methods defined lower in the same mock. The test therefore never exercises the real event-triggering code added to `ContentDefinitionManager.cs` — it can pass or fail independent of whether that production code is correct. Rewrite the test to drive the actual `ContentDefinitionManager` (with a fake `IContentDefinitionStore`) so the new trigger logic is genuinely covered.

4. **`ContentDefinitionManager.cs` constructor**: it now has a hard dependency on `IEnumerable<IContentDefinitionEventHandler>`, a type this same PR marks `[Obsolete("...")]`. Referencing an `[Obsolete]` type directly from core framework code will raise CS0618 at every build (likely breaking CI under this repo's warnings-as-errors settings) and permanently wires the "temporary" compatibility shim into the core manager rather than isolating it (e.g. behind a local `#pragma warning disable CS0618` or a small adapter class).

5. **`global.json`**: entire file rewritten for line-ending/EOF-newline differences only (CRLF→LF, trailing newline removed), unrelated to this PR's purpose. Revert this file to avoid unrelated churn and restore the trailing newline.

6. **`ContentDefinitionManager.cs` — Store/Delete methods**: the `_handlers.Invoke(...); _eventHandlers.Invoke(...);` pair is duplicated inline in every method, despite the PR description claiming dedicated "event trigger methods" were added. Extract a single private helper (e.g. `TriggerEvent<TContext>(Action<IContentDefinitionHandler,TContext>, Action<IContentDefinitionEventHandler,TContext>, TContext)`) so behavior doesn't drift as the remaining events (item 2) get wired in.

7. **New files lack a trailing newline** (`ContentDefinitionEventMigrationTests.cs`, `ContentDefinitionInterfaceTests.cs`, the migration guide `README.md`) and `ContentDefinitionEventMigrationTests.cs` mixes a file-scoped `namespace` declaration with an indented, block-bodied class — inconsistent with the repo's code style/.editorconfig. Run the formatter/dotnet-format before merge.
